headlines.article_text: Bank of America (BAC) Q3 2026 earnings Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article BAC Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Brian Moynihan, Chairman and CEO of Bank of America, speaks with Economic Club of Washington Chair David Rubenstein at an event at the Ritz-Carlton on February 25, 2025 in Washington, DC. Anna Moneymaker | Getty Images Bank of America posted a sharp decline to third-quarter profit after being hit with a $1.2 billion penalty by the U.S. Treasury Department. Shares of the bank fell more than 4% in premarket trading. Here's what the company reported: Earnings per share: 91 cents, may not compare with $1.10 LSEG estimate Revenue: $30.12 billion vs. $30.69 billion estimate The bank's profit fell 17% to $6.93 billion, or 91 cents a share. Excluding the penalty, which sapped income by 17 cents, EPS would've been $1.08 a share. Revenue rose 3.2% to $30.12 billion in the quarter, below expectations by about $570 million, largely on misses from Wall Street trading operations. Fixed income trading revenue fell 17% to $2.55 billion on weakness in mortgages, municipals, and credit activity. That is roughly $450 million below the StreetAccount estimate. Equities trading revenue climbed 10% to $2.51 billion, but that was also below analysts' expectations, by nearly $300 million. The Treasury episode, in which U.S. regulators said the company failed to report billions of dollars in suspicious transactions, will inevitably spark questions as to whether CEO Brian Moynihan has a handle on controls at the second-biggest U.S. bank by assets. Moynihan took the helm in 2010 and spent the early years of his tenure making amends for mortgage-related abuses in the aftermath of the 2008 financial crisis. Now, questions arise as to whether there are any more risk-management issues waiting to be found. The Treasury announcement adds 11th-hour intrigue to what was an otherwise fairly routine bank earnings week. On Tuesday, JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Wells Fargo posted mixed results, with JPMorgan missing EPS and revenue estimates for the first time in years. This story is developing. headlines.summary: BlackRock's assets under management — which determine a large chunk of its earnings — rose to $15.49 trillion, from $13.46 trillion a year earlier.
headlines.article_text: BlackRock profit jumps as resilient markets boost fees Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article BLK Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT The BlackRock logo is pictured outside the company's headquarters in the Manhattan borough of New York City on May 25, 2021. Carlo Allegri | Reuters BlackRock posted a jump in third-quarter profit on Wednesday, as the world's largest asset manager raked in higher fees from managing client funds. The company's shares jumped nearly 4% in premarket trading. BlackRock's profit ⁠rose to $1.66 billion, or $10.57 per share, in the three months ended September 30, compared with $1.32 billion, or $8.43 per share, a year ​earlier. Assets under management — which determine ​a large chunk of ​the earnings — rose to $15.49 trillion, from $13.46 trillion a year earlier. The growth was driven by a combination of $134.5 billion of new flows into BlackRock's flagship iShares ETFs, and the rising valuations of its investments in a robust ⁠equity ‌market. "Market fundamentals are strong and well supported, with higher ⁠margins and earnings momentum catalyzed by new technology," CEO Larry Fink said in a statement. The benchmark S&P 500, which is trading close to its all-time highs fueled by a rally in AI-focused stocks, extended its steady climb in the quarter, while ‌investors continued to demonstrate their willingness to pour money into asset management firms such as BlackRock. Even as markets have remained sturdy, the combination of surging bond yields and ​the expectation that the Federal Reserve's recent interest rate hike marks the beginning of a tightening cycle has called into question whether the rally can be sustained. Higher yields over a sustained period can put pressure on markets as investors rotate capital into safe-haven assets, ⁠locking in better risk-adjusted returns. Net flows into BlackRock's debt products were $78.2 billion in the quarter, signaling strong investor appetite despite ‌the recent steep selloff in Treasuries. Private markets push BlackRock has accelerated its ‌push into private credit markets in recent years. The asset class typically generates higher fees than the firm's main source of profits, its suite of ETFs, which depends on high volumes of inflows to boost earnings. The company ⁠has spelled out plans to deliver more than $35 billion in revenue by the end of ⁠the decade, with over 30% of that coming from private markets and technology.
